post.title: System Design Replication and Failover: Keep Services Alive When a Primary Dies
post.subtitle: A clear guide to replicas, failover detection, replica lag, and the trade-offs behind reliable database designs.
post.brief: Replication means keeping multiple copies of your data so the system can survive machine, process, or availability-zone failures. Failover is the coordinated act of promoting a healthy replica, rerouting traffic, and recovering without corrupting data.

content.markdown:
## Scenario context

Replication means keeping multiple copies of your data so the system can survive machine, process, or availability-zone failures. Failover is the coordinated act of promoting a healthy replica, rerouting traffic, and recovering without corrupting data.

> **TLDR**: If one database going down takes your product down, replication is the next design step. Failover is how you make that redundancy usable.






**How it…

This walkthrough focuses on **Lessons Learned**.

Before making a design choice, clarify:

- - Replication and failover are separate ideas: one copies data, the other restores authority.
- - Read replicas help scale reads, but they do not guarantee fresh data.
- - Asynchronous replication reduces write latency but can lose the newest acknowledged data during a crash.
